column2: Moses addresses all Israel beyond Jordan; the western wilderness setting and Paran, Tophel, Laban, Aulon and Katachrysea remain selected forms.
Eleven days links Horeb, the Mount Seir route and Kadesh-barnea; the English supplies the normal journey construction.
Year forty, month eleven, day one and all the commanded words remain explicit.
Sihon is located at Heshbon, Og at both Ashtaroth and Edrei; the two kings and all three locations remain.
Beyond Jordan in Moab, Moses begins to make the law plain, preserving the explanatory purpose.
The Lord's speech at Horeb declares their residence on this mountain sufficient; the inherited dignified imperative remains intelligible.
The route includes Arabah, hills, plain, southwest, coast, Canaan and Anti-Lebanon to Euphrates; selected Anti-Lebanon is not changed to Lebanon.
The delivered land is to be inherited under the oath to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and their descendants; all named promise recipients remain.
Moses' inability to bear Israel alone begins the leadership account, retaining the future expression.
Israel's multiplication is likened to heaven's stars, with today and the stated multitude preserved.
The blessing requests a thousandfold increase and the Lord's promised blessing; the wish remains distinct from a prediction.
Trouble, resistance and disputes remain three burdens in Moses' question.
column3: Resistance for the selected hypostasis is a contextual lexical decision needing further review; it is not treated as a settled equivalent across the corpus.

column2: Wisdom, knowledge and understanding qualify tribal leaders; all three qualities are retained.
The people's response approves doing what Moses proposed, preserving both approval and action.
The three qualifications recur, followed by commanders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens and recording officers for judges.
column3: The precise administrative role of grammatoeisagogeis requires specialist lexical review; recording officers is provisional.

column2: Judges hear cases and judge justly between a man, his brother and his sojourner; the stranger is included in the instruction.
Impartiality toward small and great, fearlessness because judgment belongs to God, and referral of difficult cases all remain.
Moses commanded all required actions at that time, closing the appointment passage.
The journey traverses the great and fearful wilderness from Horeb toward the Amorite hills to Kadesh-barnea under divine command.
Arrival at the Amorite hill country is paired with the Lord's gift to Israel.
The command to inherit includes both prohibitions of fear and dismay, retaining the ancestral promise.
All the people propose scouting the land, route and cities; both requested report subjects remain.
Moses approves and selects twelve men, one from each tribe; both counts remain.
The scouts reach the Valley of the Cluster and search it; the descriptive name is retained without importing Eshcol.
Fruit is carried in their hands and brought down; their report calls the Lord's offered land good.
Unwillingness to ascend and disobedience to the Lord's word remain two related acts.
The people's claim that the Lord hates them remains reported speech, with Egypt, Amorite hands and destruction in their accusation.
The selected your brethren and your heart remain despite the surrounding quoted question; great numbers, stronger people, heaven-high walls and sons of giants all remain.
Cowering and fearing are both prohibited, preserving the two selected verbs.
The Lord goes before Israel and Himself fights with them against the enemy, as He acted in Egypt.
The Lord's nurturing of Israel is compared to a man's nurturing his son throughout the journey; the selected nurturing verb is not reduced to physical carrying.
Israel's lack of trust concerns this matter, retaining the connection with the narrated care.
Going ahead, choosing a place, guiding in night fire and day cloud, and showing the route all remain.
The Lord hears their words, is provoked and swears, preserving the sequence of response.
The oath denies these men sight of the good land promised to their fathers; the negative oath idiom is explicit in English.
Caleb is excepted and receives the land he trod with his sons because of his attachment to the Lord's things.
Propose because of you for for your sakes: dia with the accusative states the cause of anger, while the inherited phrase can suggest benefit. Moses remains excluded as well.
Joshua, who stands beside Moses, will enter and enable Israel's inheritance; Moses must strengthen him.
Every young child without present knowledge of good or evil is included in entry, gift and inheritance; no additional captivity clause is imported.
The others must turn and camp in the wilderness toward the Red Sea, preserving camp rather than merely travel.
Confession, the stated resolve to fight, individual weapons and collective ascent remain, without treating the resolve as obedience after the warning.
The prohibitions of ascent and battle, divine absence and selected negative you shall not be crushed are retained without reversing the final clause.
column3: The relation of the final emphatic negative to the prohibitions needs syntactic review; it is not silently turned into a positive defeat prediction.

column2: They refuse Moses' warning, transgress the Lord's word and force their way up, retaining all three acts.
The Amorites pursue like bees and wound Israel from Seir to Hormah; the selected wounded verb remains.
Sitting and weeping are followed by the Lord neither hearing nor attending, preserving both negatives.
The repeated many-days expression at Kadesh remains, without inventing a numerical duration.
Israel turns toward the Red Sea wilderness and circles Mount Seir many days under the Lord's instruction.
The Lord's new speech introduces the northward turn.
The circling is declared sufficient, and northward movement is commanded.
Esau's descendants in Seir will fear and be very wary of Israel; selected third-person agency is not changed to an instruction for Israel to be careful.
War is forbidden and not even a footstep of land is granted, because Seir belongs by divine gift to Esau's sons.
Food is bought for silver and water obtained by measure for silver; the selected measurement remains.
The Lord our God has blessed Israel's work; consider the wilderness journey, forty years of presence and lack of want all remain.
The route passes Esau's descendants by Arabah from Ailon and Ezion-geber before turning toward Moab's wilderness.
Hostility and war against Moab are forbidden; the selected Seir given to Lot's sons remains, without harmonization to Ar.
The earlier Emim are great, numerous and strong like the Anakim; all three descriptions remain.
The people are counted as Rephaim like the Anakim and called Emim by Moabites, preserving the distinction between classification and local name.
Esau's sons replace the Horites in Seir, compared with Israel's inheritance; destruction, removal and settlement all remain.
The command and fulfillment of passing the Ravine Zered both remain in one unit.
Thirty-eight years run from Kadesh-barnea to Zered, until the entire fighting generation dies out as God swore.
God's hand consumes the generation from camp until its fall is complete, retaining the stated agency.
The death of all the warriors from among the people sets up the next divine speech.
The Lord speaks to Moses after that generational transition.
The selected Moab boundary designation Seir is retained, not replaced by a familiar alternative.
Israel approaches Ammon but may neither act as an enemy nor wage war, because the land is allotted to Lot's sons.
The land is reckoned Rephaim territory and its earlier inhabitants are called Zamzummim by Ammonites; both names remain.
The earlier nation is mightier than you, like the Anakim; the Lord destroys it before the Ammonites who inherit and settle until this day.
The selected plural they did and they blotted out remain in the comparison involving Esau's sons and Horites.
column3: The plural subjects and reference of for the sons of Esau require further syntactic review; they are not silently changed to a singular divine subject.

column2: Hivites, settlements to Gaza, Cappadocians and Cappadocia remain the selected ethnic and geographical forms, without replacing them from a different textual tradition.
Arnon is crossed, Sihon and his land are handed over, and inheritance and battle begin; the change from prohibited wars to this command remains.
Begin is an imperative to the addressee in the selected text; hearing the name brings disturbance and pangs among all nations under heaven.
Messengers are sent from Kedemoth to Sihon with words of peace; the peaceful proposal remains explicit.
The request promises passage along the way with no deviation right or left.
Food and water will be bought for silver, and passage is on foot; the paired purchase clauses remain.
Esau's sons in Seir and Moabites in Aroer are the cited precedents, with Jordan crossing and the promised land as the destination.
The Lord hardens Sihon's spirit and strengthens his heart, with delivery into Israel's hands as the stated purpose; the two verbs remain distinct.
The Lord has begun handing over Sihon and his land, and Israel is commanded to begin inheriting it; the repetition remains.
Sihon and all his people come out to battle at Jahaz, retaining king, people and location.
The Lord delivers Sihon, and Israel strikes him, his sons and all his people; all groups remain.
Every city in succession, women and children are destroyed, and none are retained alive as captives; the violent scope is not softened.
Propose livestock for cattle: the selected generic ktene covers domestic livestock, whereas current English cattle ordinarily narrows it to bovines. The exception and city spoil remain.
From Aroer and the ravine city to Gilead, no city escapes; the Lord delivers all into Israel's hands.
Ammon's land, Jabbok-adjoining territory and hill-country towns are excluded according to the Lord's command, preserving the stated territorial exception.
